target_fields.title_text: Minority Game and Volatility Clustering in Financial Markets
target_fields.abstract_text: We demonstrate that the Minority Game model reproduces volatility clustering in financial time series. The model assumes that market participants have bounded rationality and finite memory capacity. Using this framework, we simulate synthetic return series from inductive choice parameters. However, multi-asset extension suffers from exponential state space growth.

target_fields.title_text: Hawkes Process Calibration for High-Frequency Order Flow Imbalance
target_fields.abstract_text: We calibrate mutually exciting Hawkes processes to model high-frequency order flow imbalance. We employ Maximum Likelihood Estimation to recover baseline intensities and excitation matrices. The model predicts short-term mid-price movements from limit order arrivals. We assume that order events follow Poisson point dynamics with exponential kernels.

target_fields.title_text: Limit Order Book Dynamic Regimes using Deep Transformer-XL
target_fields.abstract_text: We propose a deep Transformer-XL architecture to detect hidden market regimes in limit order books. The model processes multi-level orderbook snapshots to infer discrete latent volatility states. The primary limitation is computational latency during real-time inference.

target_fields.title_text: Neural Posterior Estimation for Agent-Based Financial Microstructure Models
target_fields.abstract_text: We introduce Neural Posterior Estimation (NPE) to calibrate intractable agent-based market models. NPE learns an amortized mapping from simulated return statistics to agent behavior parameters. We assume that synthetic simulations accurately encompass the true data generating process.

target_fields.title_text: Simulation-Based Inference with Neural Density Estimation for Complex Physical Systems
target_fields.abstract_text: Simulation-based inference (SBI) enables Bayesian parameter estimation without likelihood evaluation. We apply Sequential Neural Posterior Estimation (SNPE) to stochastic differential equations in fluid turbulence. The method yields accurate posterior distributions for physical transport parameters.
